newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down, in need of a lift.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down, in need of a lift.

text.p: Singapore shares closed down on Wednesday with dealers hopeful that economic data due from the U.S. overnight and Singapore on Thursday could supply the market with some much needed uplift.
"There's not much here to excite the market -- we need a lift," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index closed down 3.73 at 2,120.56, slipping back from an intra-day high of 2,128.33.
The mainly Malaysian share-tracking UOB over-the-counter index followed suit, down 3.25 at 1,298.47.
"I don't see too much more downside in Singapore. I think investors are more patient than reluctant and are waiting for an upturn in confidence," another dealer said.
Traded volume reflected the hesitancy with 197.1 million shares changing hands to give 182 gainers and 194 losers.
Gains were led by Singapore Press foreign shares, up Singapore $1.50 at S$27.80, with losers topped by the ASEAN Fund 200 investment fund, down US$0.30 at US$18.50.
A loss of US$0.26 to US$2.94 for Taiwan-based Want Want came on news that Taiwan was clamping down on China investment, on which the firm depends, dealers said.
